source: ASHRAE (2019) HVAC Applications Handbook Chapter 49 Tables 29 to 34, PDF pages 914-916 (printed pp. 49.30-49.32)
about:
Forty-six sheet-metal duct walls over the six tables of the chapter that measure one: Tables 29, 30 and 31 give TLout, the sound that leaves a duct through its wall, for rectangular, round and flat oval ducts, and Tables 32, 33 and 34 give TLin, the sound that enters the same wall from the room. The chapter defines TLout on folio 49.29 as “normalized duct breakout transmission loss (independent of S and A), dB” and TLin on folio 49.31 as “duct break-in transmission loss, dB”.

One row here is one printed row, and the two quantities are two rows and never two columns of one. The round tables settle it: Table 30 measures ducts of 200, 350, 560 and 810 mm at 4.6 m and Table 32 ducts of 203, 356, 559 and 813 mm at 4.57 m, and their spiral blocks share not one diameter and not one length, 300, 610 and 915 mm at 3.6, 7.3 and 3 m against 203, 356, 660 and 813 mm all at 3.05 m, so there is no construction to carry both numbers. The rectangular and flat oval tables do print the same seven sizes, row for row and each at the same gauge as its twin, but the page never says the specimen was the same one, and a catalogue that merged them would be making that claim on the chapter's behalf.

Nothing here was converted. This is the SI edition, so the sizes are printed in millimetres, the lengths in metres and the values in decibels. Two cells are carried and no other is: the diameter of the two rows of Table 30 whose cell the page leaves blank, carried down from the row above and recorded in carried, naming the row that prints it. The gauge is the one column that is neither: the chapter prints a US sheet-metal gauge number and converts exactly one of the six these tables use, “16 ga (1.6 mm thickness)” in the running text of folio 49.37, with nothing anywhere for the 18, 20, 22, 24 and 26 the same tables print, so the gauge is held exactly as it is printed, asterisk and all, and no thickness is invented for it.

Two kinds of cell hold no value, and a third holds one with a mark on it. A cell written “>45” is a lower bound: it is held as a range whose printed end is the 45 the page gives and whose other end is left empty, because a transmission loss has no ceiling and a number put there to stand for one would be read as a measurement, and it is flagged bounded_below so that no reader takes the bound for a value. A cell printed as an em-dash is held as unquantified with the glyph the page prints, because the page prints no legend for that mark anywhere and reading it as “not measured” would be inventing one. A cell written “(53)” is a value, and the parentheses are a mark the Table 32 note does explain: “Parentheses indicate measurements in which background sound produced greater uncertainty than usual.” That is not what any hedge of this catalogue means, and in particular it is not approximate, which is a number an author rounded on purpose, so the value is held exactly as printed and the mark is recorded in the row's note. Counted on the pages: Table 30 has four bounds and two parenthesised values, Table 32 has thirteen bounds and two parenthesised values, and Tables 31 and 34 have twenty-three em-dashes each.

Two readers transcribed the six tables from the rendered pages without seeing each other's work and agreed on every data cell. Table 34 is printed twice, complete, on folio 49.31 and again on folio 49.32; the two printings were compared row by row and mark by mark, they agree, and one set of seven rows is kept. In Table 30 one printed diameter covers three rows: 610 mm is printed on the first of them and the two below it leave the cell blank, so those two rows carry it down and say in carried which row prints it.
conventions: Table 32 note, the only legend printed for a censored cell anywhere on folios 49.30 to 49.32, and the one Table 30's own marks are read by: “Note: In cases where background sound swamped sound radiated from duct walls, a lower limit on TLin is indicated by >. Parentheses indicate measurements in which background sound produced greater uncertainty than usual.”
Table 29 note, printed word for word again under Table 31: “Note: Data are for duct lengths of 6.1 m, but values may be used for cross section shown regardless of length.”
Table 33 note, printed again under both printings of Table 34: “Note: Data are for duct lengths of 6.1 m.”
Table 30 footnote, whose marker is the asterisk on two gauge cells: “*Ducts internally lined with 25 mm thick 24 kg/m3 fiberglass with 0.6 mm perforated sheet metal inner liner.”
The em-dashes of Tables 31 and 34 have no legend. Nothing on folios 49.30 to 49.32 says what the mark means, and the Table 32 note covers the bound and the parentheses only.
